question.text: The d-electronic configuration of  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced close="]" open="["><msub><mi>CoCl</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> in tetrahedral crystal field is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></msup><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></msubsup></math>. The sum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and number of unpaired electrons is

solution.text:
The oxidation state of Co in complex CoCl42- is

x-4=-2

x=+2

Electronic configuration of Co is  C27o=Ar4s23d7

So, Co+2=[Ar]3d7

Since Cl- is a weak field ligand, so the given complex will have a tetrahedral geometry with following Crystal-field splitting

 

So, value of (m)+(unpaired electrons) is (4)+(3)=7.
